Closing. Change 1997 MERGED as `83f0757b12`, which is the tip of `origin/main` — submitted
unchanged (my rebase meant Gerrit needed no server-side rebase). LLM-Review +1 AND Verified +1.

## The confound, and why it is the load-bearing part of this RCA

Every prior observation of this failure came from a full-suite run on a SATURATED host. Load and
suite-breadth were therefore confounded in 100% of the evidence, and "passes alone, fails in the
suite" cannot by itself distinguish cross-tier pollution from resource contention from generic
ordering dependence. Three separations broke it:

1. **Order, holding everything else fixed.** The SAME two files, same host, same load, only the
   order reversed: polluter-then-target fails 6/6; target-then-polluter passes. Co-presence is
   not the variable and load is not the variable — import ORDER is, and it is sufficient.
2. **Load, holding order fixed.** `tests/interfaces/facades` (577 tests, target included) under
   DELIBERATE saturation (24 spinners, load average 43-48) -> 576 passed, 1 skipped, 0 failed,
   in 546s versus ~5s quiet. A 100x slowdown produced ZERO failures. Load is neither necessary
   nor sufficient.
3. **Suite breadth is irrelevant.** The deterministic reproduction is TWO files and ~10 seconds
   on a quiet host. No full suite required.

Hypothesis 2 (resource contention) is rejected. Hypothesis 3 (generic ordering dependence — xdist
worker assignment, shared tmp path, random seed) is refined out: reversing two files flips the
result, so it is one named seam, not a scheduling artifact. Hypothesis 1 survives, with the
polluter named: any earlier test importing `rebar_reconciler.access_check` — in the full suite,
`tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/test_preflight_project_visibility.py`, since `tests/unit` runs first.
Within `tests/interfaces` alone the only other importer is
`facades/test_bridge_vocabulary_e2e_heldout.py`, and "programmatic" sorts before "vocabulary" —
which is exactly why the tier passed in isolation.

## Fail-open instance (the third in this one investigation)

The original bug is itself a fail-open: a frozen import default meant a `pytest.mark.unit` test
silently issued LIVE Jira calls instead of using its fake, and reported a plausible-looking FAIL
rather than announcing that its injection seam had missed. The runtime probe caught it creating
and querying real issue keys. The other two seen this session: the optionality CI step, which
failed fast on a missing file with `collected 0 items` and no assertion that anything ran; and my
own progress monitor, whose sentinel could never fire on a contended host, so it timed out
silently. All three fail quietly and fast, and all three read as a different failure than they
are. Feeding this to `sphinxian-agrarian-snake`.

## Acceptance criteria — evidence per tick

- AC1 deterministic reproduction: 6/6 on two files, ~10s, quiet host. Command in the RCA comment.
- AC2 named changeable artifact: `access_check.py:14` (by-value import) + `:99` (frozen default).
  Not "flakiness", not "an environment issue".
- AC3 RED before fix: `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/test_access_check_client_seam.py`, seen RED for
  the right reason ("the probe did not use the patched client class", assert 0 == 1), held OUT of
  the fix subagent's tree, GREEN after, and returned to RED by a defect-seeded mutation.
- AC4 fixes the CLASS: both frozen-default sites in the file (`:99` and `:396`) were fixed, not
  just the one the test hits. Codebase swept on two axes; three further latent seams filed as
  `freezing-smooth-godwit` rather than fixed in a bug fix's scope.
- AC5 full suite passes repeatedly: TWO full CI runs with the fix present — patchset 1 (all test
  lanes green; its only red was the unrelated optionality step, which ran ZERO tests) and
  patchset 2 (fully green, Verified +1 on the exact merged tree). Plus the targeted repro 3/3 and
  facades 576/576 under saturation. Recorded honestly: my local back-to-back double sweep was cut
  short at 44% with zero failures once CI's Verified +1 landed on the merged tree and superseded
  it — so the "repeatedly" claim rests on the two CI runs, not on two completed local sweeps.

## Attribution

`caused_by` -> `f789-3f9d-8b35-4e0d` (uncheered-sombre-bumblebee), class `plan_defect`.
Commit `fa1bf13845` (2026-08-10) CREATED both `access_check.py` and
`test_bridge_programmatic_e2e_heldout.py`, so the seam and the test that cannot reliably reach it
shipped together; the test was green at authoring only by import-order luck. An OMISSION, not a
regression — `git log -L 99,99` shows the line was never modified, so nothing broke it; the
isolation was never established. Divergence from the default worth recording: a whole-file blame
majority would name a much later toucher (1e9078f47a / 40b8ac8295, both 2026-08-18 refactors);
line-scoped blame names f789.
